0.long_answer: Klinefelter syndrome, also known as 47,XXY, is a chromosomal anomaly in males characterized by the presence of one or more extra X chromosomes. This genetic condition commonly results in infertility due to small, poorly functioning testicles and reduced testosterone production. Low testosterone levels contribute to the development of gynecomastia, which is an enlargement of the breast tissue in men. Additional clinical manifestations may include tall stature, sparse body hair, and sometimes learning or behavioral difficulties. Diagnosis is typically confirmed through a karyotype analysis that reveals the extra X chromosome.
